text:
Jordan (oncall): :rotating_light: Seeing sustained provisioning throttles in eu-west2 GPU pool, latency creeping for hosted inference. Autoscaler logs show repeated quota denies. Can someone take a look and advise traffic-shift/handoff?
PagerBot: [ALERT] eu-west2-gpu-pool THROUGHPUT_DEGRADED (severity: high) — 87% utilization, 45s p95 latency increase. Paging: Jordan (oncall), Priya (sre).
Mateo (infra): looking. initial read: cloud quotas hitting per-project vGPU soft limits, plus a few new instances stuck in PROVISIONING. see small log snippet:```ERROR: AllocateGPUs: quotaExceeded: requested 8, available 2
Trace: provisioning/retry.go:128```
Priya (sre): copy. if quota is the bottleneck we should avoid mass reprovisions — recommend traffic shift to eu-west1 and us-west2 as short-term. Mateo, can you produce a safe rollout command so we don't thundering-herd?
Mateo (infra): yep. propose staged shift: 20% -> 40% -> 60% with 5m evaluation windows. CLI: `redwoodctl traffic shift --from eu-west2 --to eu-west1,us-west2 --percent 20 --step 20 --wait 300s`
Lina (eng): fyi some customer routes are pinned to eu-west2 for data locality. we need to exclude them from shift. can we route by route tag?
Mateo (infra): good catch — use `--exclude-tags=gdpr,eu-sensitive` to keep pinned routes.
Jordan (oncall): doing the first 20% now. starting shift command.
DevOps Bot: deploybot: rollout started for traffic-shift-job-1828. Monitor: https://console/redwood/rollouts/1828
Priya (sre): while traffic shifts, we should tweak PagerBot escalation to avoid waking multiple oncall layers. Propose: during cluster-provisioning incidents, suppress secondary pager for 10m unless error rate increases.
Jordan (oncall): agree. current noise is from repeated retries causing duplicate pages. what's the config path?
Priya (sre): `pagerbot config set incident.provisioning.secondary_delay 600` — run as admin.
Lina (eng): +1. also suggest enabling failback to dedicated pools for critical routes: `--fallback=dedicated-highprio` so critical customer traffic stays up.
Mateo (infra): applied the exclude-tags and fallback flags; starting step 1 -> 20%. watch p95 and queue length.
PagerBot: [INFO] Traffic shift 20% complete. Latency p95 in eu-west2 reduced from 920ms -> 760ms. eu-west1 p95 increased 120ms -> 180ms.
Jordan (oncall): stepping to 40% after 6m — no new pagers.
Priya (sre): I've pushed the temporary PagerBot escalation tweak. It will suppress secondaries for provisioning incidents for 10m. Documenting change in incident playbook.
Mateo (infra): stepping to 60% now. note: we're seeing a few `instance_stuck` in provider API — escalating to cloud support but traffic shift is absorbing load.
Lina (eng): running a quick verification on pinned routes — all good. critical customers on fallback dedicated pool, responses within SLO.
DevOps Bot: support-ticket created: #CLOUD-9832 referencing eu-west2 provisioning, assigned to provider ops.
Jordan (oncall): good. handoff note for next oncall: provisioning quota root cause likely provider-side rate limiting and per-project quotas. action items: 1) follow up with provider ops on ticket CLOUD-9832; 2) review project's vGPU quota allocation for eu-west2; 3) consider pre-warming dedicated pool for business hours.
Priya (sre): I'm staying on until handoff in 30m to monitor rollback risk and ensure PagerBot revert. I'll revert the `secondary_delay` after stabilization.
Mateo (infra): also adding a short-term automation: if provisioning error rate > 15% for 10m, auto-shift additional 20% (capped at 80%). will PR the rule.
Jordan (oncall): thanks all. summarizing: traffic shifted to eu-west1/us-west2 with exclude-tags and dedicated fallback, PagerBot secondary suppressed for 10m, cloud ticket opened. No further pages for 25m. handing off to Priya for overnight monitoring. :thumbsup:
Priya (sre): acknowledged — taking handoff. final note: oncall runbook updated with the temp pager tweak and traffic-shift snippet.
PagerBot: [RESOLVE] eu-west2-gpu-pool THROUGHPUT_DEGRADED — condition improved. Incident closed by automation at 1828058472.
